answers.answer: LHS − RHS = a² + 4b² − 4ab = a² − 4ab + 4b² = (a − 2b)² ≥ 0, so a² + 4b² ≥ 4ab. Equality holds when a − 2b = 0, i.e. a = 2b.
Both sides are positive (a,b>0). (LHS)² − (RHS)² = (a²+b²)/2 − (a+b)²/4 = (2a²+2b² − a² − 2ab − b²)/4 = (a−b)²/4 ≥ 0. Hence (LHS)² ≥ (RHS)², so √((a²+b²)/2) ≥ (a+b)/2. Equality holds when a = b.
Yes, equality holds (when a = b). Since a>0, b>0, by AM-GM b/a + a/b ≥ 2√((b/a)(a/b)) = 2√1 = 2. Equality holds when b/a = a/b, i.e. a² = b², so a = b (both positive).
